Title:
Read Deep, Write Shallow: How Looped Language Models Should Spend Their Depth

Authors:
Yang Hu

Primary category: cs.CL (Computation and Language)
Cross-list: cs.LG (Machine Learning)

Comments:
11 pages, 5 figures. Code, per-item results and a script that recomputes every number: https://github.com/yanghu819/read-deep-write-shallow

License: CC BY 4.0

Abstract (plain text):
Looped language models reuse one block of layers several times per token and usually spend the same number of loops reading the prompt and writing the answer. We show that the two buy different things: depth spent reading the prompt mainly buys knowledge and long-context accuracy, while depth spent writing the answer mainly buys multi-step derivation. To measure this, a small connector trained on a frozen looped model lets the prompt be read with p loops and the answer written with d loops, one set of parameters serving all 16 pairs up to four loops on Ouro-2.6B. With the writer fixed, reading deeper improves knowledge and long-context benchmarks on five checkpoints from two model families. On Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, reading four loops and writing two beats the native four-loop model on long-context HELMET by 4.3 points, and on GSM8K a two-loop writer answers in 0.55x its time, 1.0 point below it on the full test set. A RoPE-commuting key map lets one stored prompt KV cache serve every writing loop exactly. Linear probes find the next token more, and in Ouro the previous token less, linearly decodable from later loops' value cache. Code: https://github.com/yanghu819/read-deep-write-shallow
